chunks: And do not invoke blessings upon any of them who die, nor stand to pray at their graves; indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and they died while they were transgressors.

key_terms.فَاسِقُونَ: Transgressors / Those who deviate from divine law

ai.seo_question: Who are the people for whom the Prophet should not pray funeral prayers according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as referring specifically to the hypocrites (Munafiqun) of Medina, particularly Abu Lu'aba and his companions, whose outward piety masked inner disbelief. The prohibition on standing at their graves signifies a complete severance of communal spiritual connection, distinguishing their state from that of general disbelievers who may still receive funeral prayers. This ruling underscores the principle that major transgression (Fisq) combined with confirmed disbelief renders one unworthy of the Prophet's intercessory prayer.
